title: Towards Large Reasoning Models: A Survey of Reinforced Reasoning with Large Language Models
actual_read_scope: Read the complete arXiv HTML v3 (36 pages; sections 1-10, tables/figures captions, discussion, conclusion, and references). Extraction is limited to the survey's own summaries and bibliographic entries; cited papers were not opened.

routes.problem: Reasoning supervision is expensive, especially step-level labels.
routes.mechanism: Move from human outcome/process annotation to LLM-generated trajectories, external verification, Monte Carlo continuation, MCTS, and feedback/self-refinement; select high-quality paths or labels for SFT/PRM/RL.
routes.inference_token_link: Indirect-to-direct: search generates extra train-time traces, while the resulting PRM/policy can guide best-of-N, beam, tree search or deliberate CoT at inference. The survey does not establish deployment-token savings; search itself increases inference compute.

routes.problem: Outcome-only rewards are sparse for multi-step reasoning.
routes.mechanism: Process supervision/PRMs assign stepwise values; PRM-guided RL, SFT, DPO, or iterative policy-PRM self-training turn search traces into learned reasoning behavior.
routes.inference_token_link: Direct but unquantified: a learned policy may produce more reliable reasoning in one rollout, while the same PRM can spend more test-time tokens searching. This survey gives no Pareto curve of accuracy versus generated tokens after internalization.

routes.problem: Reasoning quality can scale with both post-training compute and inference compute.
routes.mechanism: The survey frames a reinforced cycle: search creates data, learning internalizes it, and PRM/search performs test-time deliberation; it connects RL-driven train-time scaling with search-based test-time scaling.
routes.inference_token_link: Direct conceptual link: more deliberate test-time tokens can improve accuracy, but this is a compute/token tradeoff, not evidence of fewer deployment tokens. The survey explicitly says CoT/ToT generally increase token consumption and overhead.

routes.problem: Direct-answer decoding is unreliable on complex tasks.
routes.mechanism: CoT, self-consistency, ToT/GoT, ReAct, decomposition prompts, and PRM-guided best-of-N/beam/tree search elicit or select multiple reasoning paths.
routes.inference_token_link: Direct: deliberate reasoning and multi-path search spend more test-time tokens; selection can improve accuracy. No claim of token reduction or learned early exit is made.

routes.problem: Reasoning can improve through interaction, reflection, and retained experience.
routes.mechanism: Verbal reinforcement/self-correction, memory-based reinforcement, and agentic workflow use critiques, trajectories, or memories to revise future actions/solutions.
routes.inference_token_link: Indirect/direct: extra reflection, tool calls, and agent turns raise test-time token/compute demand; memory may alter future path quality, but the survey does not measure token-normalized gains.

candidates.title: Let's Verify Step by Step
candidates.reason: Human stepwise process labels/PRM are presented as the foundation for dense supervision; relevant to internalizing reasoning, without deployment-token evidence.

candidates.title: Improve Mathematical Reasoning in Language Models by Automated Process Supervision
candidates.reason: OmegaPRM/MCTS-style automated process supervision is used for trajectory selection and PRM construction; PRM is also deployed for test-time search.

candidates.title: Math-Shepherd: Verify and Reinforce LLMs Step-by-Step without Human Annotations
candidates.reason: The survey lists label-free/process-verifier approaches as automated step supervision; internalization is relevant, but no token-normalized inference result is reported here.

candidates.title: Multi-Step Problem Solving through a Verifier: An Empirical Analysis on Model-Induced Process Supervision
candidates.reason: Monte Carlo continuation evaluates intermediate steps from final outcomes for automated process labels; primarily training-data construction.

candidates.title: LLM Self-Training via Process Reward Guided Tree Search
candidates.reason: Rest-MCTS* mutually updates policy and PRM using process-reward-guided tree search; the survey explicitly links its loop to both training and test-time search.

candidates.title: Reinforced Self-Training (ReST) for Language Modeling
candidates.reason: Survey cites self-training as a route for feeding decomposed reasoning signals back into the model; deployment token impact is not established.

candidates.title: Training Language Models to Self-Correct via Reinforcement Learning
candidates.reason: RL-trained self-correction is positioned as both post-training reasoning improvement and a test-time feedback pattern; reflection tokens add inference cost.

candidates.title: VinePPO: Unlocking RL Potential for LLM Reasoning through Refined Credit Assignment
candidates.reason: Included in the survey's multi-step RL discussion as refined credit assignment; it concerns learning efficiency/credit, not a deployment token guarantee.

candidates.title: Reasoning with Reinforced Fine-Tuning
candidates.reason: Survey places ReFT among reinforcement fine-tuning methods for reasoning; bibliography gives venue/year but no arXiv ID.

candidates.title: Scaling LLM Test-Time Compute Optimally Can Be More Effective than Scaling Model Parameters
candidates.reason: Survey uses it to motivate test-time scaling laws and optimal allocation; it is a performance-versus-test-compute relation, not token saving.

candidates.title: OpenR: An Open Source Framework for Advanced Reasoning with Large Language Models
candidates.reason: Survey explicitly maps MCTS data construction, GRPO post-training, and PRM deployment with best-of-N/beam/majority vote, linking internalization and inference search.

candidates.title: O1 Replication Journey: A Strategic Progress Report–Part 1
candidates.reason: Training-centric journey learning uses trial-and-error/reflection/backtracking data; survey notes weaker inference-stage adaptation, a useful contrast for train/test coupling.

candidates.title: Llama-Berry: Pairwise Optimization for O1-like Olympiad-level Mathematical Reasoning
candidates.reason: Survey characterizes SR-MCTS, pairwise preference reward, and Borda aggregation as inference-focused reasoning optimization; inference search increases tokens.

candidates.title: Reflexion: Language Agents with Verbal Reinforcement Learning
candidates.reason: Survey's verbal reinforcement section uses reflection and episodic memory as test-time improvement; no parameter update or token-saving claim is made.

candidates.title: Self-Refine: Iterative Refinement with Self-Feedback
candidates.reason: Feedback/refinement is cited as a way to improve generated annotations and test-time reasoning; iterative calls add token cost.

candidates.title: When a Language Model Is Optimized for Reasoning, Does It Still Show Embers of Autoregression? An Analysis of OpenAI o1
candidates.reason: Survey cites analyses of o1 and emphasizes unresolved mechanism/theory; useful caution against treating slow thinking or extra tokens as established internalization.

gaps_conflicts: The survey's central taxonomy is data construction -> learning to reason -> test-time scaling, but it does not define a token-normalized accuracy frontier, adaptive stopping rule, or deployment budget metric.

It repeatedly links train-time search/RL, PRM learning, and test-time search, yet evidence is heterogeneous: some systems train a policy, some only search at inference, and OpenAI o1 details remain undisclosed.

Several cited contributions reduce annotation or training burden, but that is not deployment token saving. MCTS/Monte Carlo, self-consistency, best-of-N, ToT, reflection, and agentic workflows generally add test-time tokens/compute.

The survey claims high-quality process-reward data may matter more than general pretraining size and calls slow-thinking internalization an open theoretical problem; it does not establish causal transfer from data quality to shorter reasoning traces.
Version coverage stops at v3 (2025-01-23) and therefore does not cover later 2025-2026 reasoning models, dynamic token budgets, distilled short-reasoning models, or newer verifier/early-exit work.
